### Observed differences

- In the later window, A19 and A20 appear in roughly half of all traces: A19 in about 92 of 200 traces (46 in 100) and A20 in about 111 of 200 (56 in 100), versus only about 1 and 2 of 200 traces earlier; when present, each occurs exactly once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002]
- In the later window the two are near-exclusive alternatives: about 44 in 100 traces contain A19 but not A20, about 54 in 100 contain A20 but not A19, only about 2 in 100 contain both, and about 0.5 in 100 contain neither. [REL001]
- A40's routing changed markedly: earlier, about 90 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions went to A25; in the later window about 53 in 100 go to A20 and about 42 in 100 to A19, with A25 down to about 0.5 in 100 and only small residual shares elsewhere. [DIR003]
- A19 and A20 now lead almost exclusively to A25 — about 97 in 100 of A19's observed outgoing transitions and about 96 in 100 of A20's — whereas their earlier routing (A19 to A29; A20 to A21/A23) rested on only 1–2 observations. [DIR001, DIR002]
- Order relations line up with this: in the later window A19 precedes A25 in about 46 in 100 traces and follows A40 in about 45 in 100; A20 precedes A25 in about 55 in 100 and follows A40 in about 56 in 100 — together covering essentially every trace containing one of them. [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]
- The observed distance from A40 to A25 grew from one step in about 90 in 100 traces to two steps in about 93 in 100 (three steps in about 7 in 100). [LAG001]
- Positions are consistent: A19 and A20 sit at a mean relative event position of about 0.36 in the later window, while A25 — present in every trace in both windows — sits slightly later than before (mean about 0.38 vs about 0.40). [POS001, POS002, POS003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, one of two near-exclusive alternative steps — A19 in about 46 in 100 cases, A20 in about 54 in 100 — is executed between A40 and A25, where previously A40 was followed directly by A25 in about 90 in 100 traces. The placement is shown directly by relational and positional evidence, not inferred from participation alone: A40's successors shifted from A25 to A19/A20, A19 and A20 now lead almost exclusively to A25, each appears after A40 and before A25 in the traces where it occurs, and the A40-to-A25 distance shifted from one step to two. Screening tested 93 units and would be expected to yield about 0.46 qualifying items if nothing had changed; the 14 items here collapse to this single coherent difference rather than many unrelated ones, and every item's difference exceeds about 199 of 200 random re-splits, making chance a poor explanation. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, LAG001, POS001, POS002, POS003, OCC001, OCC002]

Limitations remain. The before-side routing profiles of A19 and A20 rest on only 1 and 2 observed transitions (and their earlier positions on 1–2 events), so what these activities fed into previously is weakly established. The evidence also cannot fully rule out that the two windows sample different variant mixes of an unchanged process — finite samples can differ in variant frequency — although a rise from about 0.5–1 in 100 to about 46–56 in 100 traces, with consistent relational shifts, is far outside what random re-splits produce. DIR shares are computed over outgoing transitions rather than cases, and POS/LAG use event positions rather than clock time. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, POS001, POS002, LAG001]
